title: Australia Skilled Worker Visa 2026: Points & Requirements
metaDescription: Australia skilled worker visa 2026: 65+ points test, Subclass 189/190/491 explained, skills assessment, EOI via SkillSelect, costs and processing times.
headline: Australia Skilled Worker Visa 2026: Points & Requirements

sections.content:
Australia's General Skilled Migration program offers permanent residency to skilled workers without requiring an employer sponsor. The three points-tested pathways are Subclass 189 for independent migrants who can live anywhere, Subclass 190 for state-nominated migrants, and Subclass 491 for regional provisional visa holders.

Alongside these, the employer-sponsored Skills in Demand visa (Subclass 482) provides a faster non-points route for workers with a nominated position from an approved Australian employer. All pathways can lead to permanent residence for the applicant and included family members.
sections.title: Skilled Migration Pathways Overview

sections.content:
The points test decides who gets invited. You need at least 65 points, though competitive rounds favor scores of 80 or more. Age 25 to 32 earns the maximum 30 points, superior English earns 20, and skilled employment adds up to 20 points across Australian and overseas experience.

Education contributes 15 to 20 points depending on the qualification level. State nomination adds 5 points for Subclass 190 and 15 for Subclass 491, while partner skills, Australian study, specialist education and credentialed community language add further points.
sections.title: The Points Test Explained

sections.content:
Before applying, you need a positive skills assessment from the authority for your occupation, such as ACS for ICT professionals, Engineers Australia for engineers, or VETASSESS for trades. You also need competent English, demonstrated through IELTS, PTE or an accepted equivalent.

You then submit an Expression of Interest through SkillSelect. If invited, you have 60 days to lodge the full application with health examinations, police clearances, employment references and the visa fee, which starts around 4,115 Australian dollars for the primary applicant.
sections.title: Skills Assessment and How to Apply

sections.content:
Skilled independent and nominated visa processing typically takes six to twelve months from invitation to grant, while the Skills in Demand visa often completes in one to three months. Complete documentation and in-demand occupations move fastest.

Beyond the visa fee, budget for skills assessments, English tests, medical examinations and police clearances. Once granted, permanent residents access Medicare, and employers contribute superannuation toward retirement on top of salary.

faqs.a: You need a minimum of 65 points on the General Skilled Migration points test to be eligible, though invitations in competitive rounds often go to candidates scoring 80 or more. Points come from age, English ability, skilled employment, education, Australian study, partner skills and state or regional nomination.
faqs.q: How many points do I need for an Australian skilled worker visa?

faqs.a: The main points-tested visas are Subclass 189 for independent skilled migrants, Subclass 190 for state-nominated migrants, and Subclass 491 for regional sponsored migrants. The employer-sponsored Skills in Demand visa, Subclass 482, follows a separate non-points pathway with its own requirements.
faqs.q: What are the Subclass 189, 190 and 491 visas?

faqs.a: You must be under 45 years old when invited, nominate an occupation on the Skilled Occupation List, and obtain a positive skills assessment from the relevant authority such as ACS or Engineers Australia. Competent English, meaning IELTS 6.0 overall or equivalent, plus health and character clearances are also mandatory.
faqs.q: What are the basic eligibility requirements for skilled migration?

faqs.a: Processing typically takes one to three months for the employer-sponsored Skills in Demand visa, while points-tested visas like Subclass 189 and 190 take six to twelve months. Timelines vary with occupation demand, application completeness and whether further documents or medical checks are requested.
